notes.reason: The note takes one sentence literally and ignores the four sentences around it that say what Jeff means. He is talking about showing footage of study participants to his audience: right after the quoted line he says "even with that permission, we still had to blur out their faces", then "I felt like I couldn't showcase exactly what the subjects were doing as well as I wanted to", then "Here, we're going to be able to film every single subject in every study that I do, show you exactly what they're doing." So his claim is about permission to record subjects for public release, not about pointing a camera at a lifter for analysis. The note's own closing line concedes exactly that, saying the new thing is "public release of anonymized footage, not permission to film" - which is Jeff's point rather than a correction of it. The two studies it cites confirm only the uncontested part: the 2021 bench press paper timed sets from a camera recording, and the 2025 coaches' paper had coaches watch videos of trainees, both internal research footage that nobody claims was forbidden. Neither source says anything about a study releasing identifiable participant footage to the public, so the note never tests the claim Jeff actually made. Jeff would read this as a note arguing with a sentence he did not mean.
